subject: Audit & Access Logs — retention windows, exports, and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Maya Patel <compliance@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Admin <it_admin@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: audit/access log retention and export formats

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our compliance team had a couple of follow-ups specifically about Redwood's audit and access logs before we finish the vendor assessment. Could you confirm the following?

1) Retention: what are the default retention windows for (a) admin audit logs (user actions like role changes, key rotations), (b) API access logs (request metadata, IPs, headers), and (c) KV/cache-access traces if any?

2) Export: can we export logs on-demand for a given time range? Supported formats (CSV/JSON/NDJSON)? Any limits on export size or streaming options to our S3/GCS/BigQuery?

3) Deletion & erasure: if Acme requests that logs containing Acme tenant identifiers be deleted, is there a deletion workflow, and how does that interact with backups and immutable archives?

4) Residency: if we choose EU data residency, are audit logs stored in-region? If we later request cross-region export, are there controls/audit trails for those exports?

If easier, a short summary or a one-page Q&A doc would be great.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Compliance Lead, Acme Corporation
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <compliance@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: audit/access log retention and export formats

Hi Maya —

Thanks for these clear questions. I pulled together the answers below; I also attached a short CSV schema and a console-export screenshot for the UI flow. Summary up top, details below.

Summary (short):
- Default retention: hosted API logs = 90 days, admin/audit events = 2 years, access metadata = 1 year.
- Export: yes, on-demand for arbitrary ranges. Formats: NDJSON (recommended), JSON, CSV. Exports can stream to S3/GCS or be downloaded from the Console/API.
- Deletion: we support targeted deletion for tenant-scoped identifiers; deletion requests go through an audit workflow and are reflected in export results once completed. Backups have separate retention and are expunged according to policy; we maintain an immutable audit trail of deletion operations.
- Residency: logs are stored in-region for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted tiers have configurable region selection and exports include provenance metadata.

Full details:
1) Retention windows (defaults and options)
- Hosted (standard):
  • API request/access logs (tokenized request metadata, IPs, headers): default 90 days; configurable up to 730 days for Enterprise plans.
  • Admin/audit logs (console actions, role changes, API key ops): default 2 years; immutable retention extensions available for Compliance add-on.
  • KV/cache-access traces: retained 30 days by default (used for performance debugging), can be disabled or extended.
- Dedicated/Private:
  • Customers can request custom retention windows as part of their contract; logs are stored per the dedicated configuration/contract.

2) Export capabilities
- On-demand exports via Console (Logs > Exports) and Programmatic API (POST /v1/logs/export).
- Supported formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), standard JSON arrays, and CSV (schema provided; see attached CSV).
- Destinations: S3, GCS, Azure Blob, or direct download. For BigQuery we provide a push connector (writes to a supplied dataset) or an NDJSON export suitable for import.
- Size/throughput: For very large ranges we provide chunked streaming exports; single-request exports are subject to the same rate limits as other exports — typical SLA-backed flows are available for Enterprise (we can provision background export workers).
- Export provenance: each export produces a manifest file with export_id, start/end times, region, and the KMS key id used to encrypt the payload.

3) Deletion/erasure workflow
- Tenant-level deletion: we support scoped erasure of tenant identifiers in logs. The steps are:
  1. Customer submits a deletion request (Console/API) with filters (tenant_id, user_id, time range).
  2. Internal review job validates filters and schedules the deletion job.
  3. Deletion job rewrites affected shards to remove tenant-identifying fields, updates live index, and records a deletion event in our immutable deletion-audit ledger (cannot be removed).
- Backups & immutable archives: backups are retained per retention policy; deletion jobs will also schedule expungement from backups if within the backup window. For records in immutable, WORM-style archives we will coordinate as per contract — typically we maintain a deletion marker and a legal hold process.
- Timing: small-range deletions complete within minutes; large-range (multi-GB/TB) jobs are queued and you get status updates via the export API/hook.

4) Residency & cross-region exports
- Hosted customers: you select a primary region for log storage at project creation; logs are kept in-region. Cross-region exports are supported but flagged in the export manifest and require admin confirmation in the Console (two-step).
- Dedicated/Private: logs remain in customer-controlled VPC/storage; export paths are controlled by the customer network/contract.
- Audit trail: every export (including cross-region) is recorded in an export-audit log with user, timestamp, export_id, target URI, and KMS key id.

Security details:
- All exports encrypted at rest with AES-256; customer-controlled KMS keys available for Dedicated/Private.
- Role-based access for log exports; exports require the export_logs permission and are logged in the admin audit stream.

Next steps:
- If you want, we can run a short test export to your S3 bucket and provide the manifest + sample NDJSON.
- Priyom — can you confirm the CSV column names and BigQuery schema I attached are correct for our export connector?

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: audit/access log retention and export formats

Thanks Hannah — quick confirmations from the export schema side. Attached CSV (redwood_audit_log_schema_v1.csv) maps to the NDJSON fields. Key points:
- CSV columns: event_time, tenant_id (hashed/encrypted when requested), user_id (pseudonymized optional), event_type, resource, action, ip_address, user_agent, request_id, export_id
- BigQuery: recommend NDJSON import for nested fields; we provide a load job and a recommended table schema (we'll share as a .sql snippet).

Note: for GDPR-driven pseudonymization we can hash tenant_id by default and provide reversible tokens when customers bring their own KMS.

Priyom
Sr. Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Hannah/Priyom —

This is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups:
- Can you confirm whether the admin/audit logs are considered part of the "immutable deletion-audit ledger"? We want proof that deletion requests were executed and cannot be suppressed.
- For tenant-scoped deletion, will exported files created before the deletion be amended/republished or do we need to request a re-export after the job completes?

Also, if possible we'd like to run a demo export to our S3 bucket next Tuesday. Vivek, can you arrange the logistics?

Thanks,
Maya
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <compliance@acme-corp.com>, IT Admin <it_admin@globex.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: audit/access log retention and export formats

Hi all — quick answers:
- The immutable deletion-audit ledger is separate from the admin/audit logs. It records metadata about deletion operations (who requested, filters used, timestamp, job id) and is WORM-protected so entries cannot be modified or removed. That ledger is what we point customers to as proof of erasure operations.
- Exports created before a deletion will not be retroactively changed. After a deletion job completes we can:
  1) re-run the export with the same filters to produce a sanitized file, or
  2) provide a deletion manifest showing which objects/rows were removed and the export_ids affected.

Vivek — please reach out to Maya to schedule the test export and confirm S3 bucket details. I'll create the support ticket and hook the export job to it so Acme has a traceable record (HS-4521).

Best,
Hannah
